va_virginia_creeper_boulder.blurb: A single compact boulder tucked between the Virginia Creeper Trail and the river in southwest Virginia, on the stretch between Damascus and Whitetop Station. It holds 13 bouldering problems: about half are V0, a few sit around V1 to V3, and a handful of traverses and harder lines reach V5. The blocks are short and the landings are good on every side, so it suits beginners, families and anyone who wants a quick session while out on a bike ride. A cleared flat spot next to it makes a handy place to rest. Most visitors treat it as a bonus stop on the trail, not a destination of its own.

va_mike_n_ike_boulder.blurb: A large, approachable boulder within the SLS Area of Grayson Highlands State Park in southwest Virginia, sitting right alongside the Listening Rock trail. Its 13 bouldering problems lean easy: roughly five at V2, a few at V0 and V1, and a small number of harder lines up to about V5. Problems are short, so this is a good stop for beginners and groups wanting a mix of grades without a long walk. The trail bends in front of the boulder after you pass the Mouth of Wilson block, which makes it simple to spot. Bring a pad for the landings.
